# Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the Boss — "The Central AI" from GDD §4.3. The scene should show its multi-phase health bar, 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases, and complex bullet patterns. This is the final challenge enemy with unique mechanics (multi-hit health, phase transitions).

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing boss behaviour — wants to see all boss attack phases, health bar, and bullet patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of multi-phase boss behaviour with health bar management.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Boss cycle through 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases so I can verify the phase transition logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to see a 4-phase health bar that visually depletes as the Boss takes damage so I can verify the health bar rendering.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to deal damage to the Boss so I can test health bar progression and phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear visual and audio cues before each boss attack phase begins so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`) renders the Boss enemy with all attack patterns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Boss visual style:** The Central AI renders as a large, imposing neon entity with a visible central core, consistent with a "boss" aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multi-phase health bar:** A 4-phase health bar is displayed; each phase depletes independently. The Boss cycles through 3–4 distinct attack patterns as health phases progress.
- [ ] **AC4 — Boss attack phases implemented:** All Boss phases from the GDD are present:
  - **Phase 1:** Spread — Boss fires bullets in a wide spread pattern.
  - **Phase 2:** Spiral — Bullets spiral outward from the Boss in a rotating pattern.
  - **Phase 3:** Pulse — Screen-wide pulse wave expands from the Boss, followed by aimed shots at the player's last known position.
  - **Phase 4 — Desperation:** All previous patterns combined at higher speed; Boss core becomes more exposed/bright (visual cue).
- [ ] **AC5 — Damage button:** A button on-screen deals damage to the Boss, advancing the health bar through phases. Visual cues (core exposure) change at each phase transition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Telegraphing:** Each attack phase begins with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the visual event.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD beyond health bar, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** The Boss is multi-hit (4 phases). Each phase has a distinct visual representation and attack pattern.
- **Phase transitions:** Visual cues (core exposure, brightness) indicate phase progression. Audio cues announce transitions.
- **Firing:** All Boss attack phases fire complex bullet patterns. Patterns should be learnable but increasingly difficult as phases progress.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, each phase's unique audio cue, phase transitions, and destruction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — The Boss gym scene.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Boss enemy entity (multi-phase health + attack patterns).
- `src/assets/` — Boss sprite (large, imposing neon entity with core).
- `src/audio/` — Boss-related sound effects (spawn, phase cues, transitions, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.3 Boss Design (The Central AI).

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library or its documented extension seam (§5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) where applicable (Boss phase/health extensions may compose with the base class) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5: `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUpsCombat`; note threat-coupled effects as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviours + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — **new** combat gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — extend the catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — extend with shield-absorb state, bomb bullet-clear, phase-shift hit suppression, teleport safe-spot resolution + FIFO consumption.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — extend with P3/P4/P6/P7 code-drawn icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **reused** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **reused unchanged** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — possibly parameterised aim target (ship position) for `tryFireAimedBullet`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` (+ P3/P4/P6/P7 unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — teleport safe radius + travelled distance, hit-reset values (extend the shared constants).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (the non-combat gym): **prerequisite** — supplies the shared PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, icons, HUD class, and spawn/lifecycle constants this item reuses/extends. Dependency edge: this item → AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling — weapon power-ups excluded here, same round-robin/grow-shrink/3% mechanics.
- **"Create E1 Scout gym scene" / GymScout** — precedent for the Scout formation, EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, and the `GymFormationScene` core-library pattern (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q completed; core-library refactor AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK / AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 completed).
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — precedent for `Player` reuse.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Redesign P7 Dash…" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V), "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — semantics source for P7/P9/P8 (P3/P4/P6 remain as defined in GDD §4.4).
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Dependency:** this item assumes the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) lands first (PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, HUD, constants). If that item is delayed, the combat scene work is blocked — do not build parallel copies of the lifecycle/HUD.
- **Assumption — ship-aimed fire:** Scout's `tryFireAimedBullet` currently aims at a fixed demo target; the combat scene requires bullets aimed at the ship's live position. Implement by parameterising the aim target (small, contained change) rather than duplicating the Scout entity.
- **Assumption — teleport safe spot:** "nearest safe spot in the travel direction" = first empty position along the travel ray where no enemy body or bullet occupies a safety-radius disc (tunable, proposal 3× ship size), clamped to screen bounds; fallback = nearest on-screen safe position (GDD); P6 granted on arrival.
- **Assumption — hit response flash/reset:** a hit without shield/phase shift flashes the ship and repositions it (or grants brief invulnerability) — exact demo values tunable; no lives, no game over (operator Q8).
- **Assumption — scout formation counts as the "low-level threat":** default V-formation of ~6 scouts with drift (as GymScout), SHOOT toggle default OFF so the operator/player can turn fire on for the demo.
- **Scope-creep guard:** E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss threats, weapon autofire, lives/score, leaderboard, and the non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9) are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling drift:** same constants/mechanics as the two sibling gyms; coordinate to keep the shared lifecycle consistent (extract a shared util if a third consumer appears).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (this round): "Which enemies constitute 'low level enemy threats' — reuse existing E1 Scout/E2 Diver/E3 Tank entities with bullet-firing, or generic placeholders?" — Answer (operator): **"1. Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene reuses the existing E1 Scout entity with its shooting enabled. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (this round): "Ship hit response in the combat gym — (a) lives with respawn (3 lives), (b) simple flash/reset without a lives counter, (c) other?" — Answer (operator): **"2. b"** — simple flash/reset, no lives counter (pure demo). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (scope split, previous round): "Separate the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) into their own work item and combat scene with low-level enemy threats?" — Answer (operator): **"Separate out the combat coupled items into a different work item and different combat scene. That scene should contain low level enemy threats."** — implemented as this item; the threat-free gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) keeps P5/P8/P9 and the shared lifecycle/HUD. Source: interactive reply.

# Extend effects module with combat-coupled power-up behaviours

## Summary
Extend `src/powerups/effects.ts` (or create it if not yet present from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) with the four combat-coupled effect implementations. Each effect function receives the scene context and ship reference, manages its own state/timer, and exposes an API for the collision pass to query state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Shield effect (shieldAbsorb):** Returns an effect object with `isActive`, `pop()` method, `apply()` that renders a bubble around the ship, `onHit()` that absorbs one hit and pops, and a timer that expires after 15s. `recollect()` refreshes timer to 15s.
- [ ] **AC2 - Bomb effect (bombClear):** Returns an effect with `apply()` that removes all on-screen enemy bullets (iterates the bullet collection and destroys each), does NOT damage enemy entities. Shows a brief HUD notice string. `recollect()` is a benign no-op.
- [ ] **AC3 - Phase Shift effect (phaseShift):** Returns an effect with `isActive`, `isInvulnerable` flag set to true during active period, `apply()` that renders a ghost outline of the ship, 3s duration timer, `recollect()` refreshes to 3s.
- [ ] **AC4 - Teleport effect (teleport):** Returns an effect with a FIFO stack of remaining uses, `consume()` removes one use and returns true if any remain, `getCount()` returns remaining uses. `apply()` triggers safe-spot resolution (see AC5). On teleport success, grants P6 Phase Shift (3s).
- [ ] **AC5 - Safe-spot resolution (resolveSafeSpot):** A pure function that takes current ship position, travel direction, enemy positions, bullet positions, and safe radius. Returns the nearest safe position along the travel ray (no enemy/bullet within safe radius), clamped to screen bounds. If no safe spot in travel direction, returns nearest on-screen safe position (GDD fallback).
- [ ] **AC6 - Effect factory:** A `createEffect(type, scene, ship)` factory function that dispatches to the correct implementation based on the power-up id.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/powerups/effects.ts` with shield, bomb, phase shift, teleport, safe-spot, and factory

## Key Files:

# When all enemies in enemy gym scene have been killed respawn them (AH-0MTFXKA5Q003LBH5)

## Problem statement

Enemy gym scenes (`GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm`) allow the player to destroy every enemy (1 HP each, `alive === false` after `destroySelf()`), leaving an empty field with nothing to do. When the formation is fully cleared, start a visible 3-second countdown and then respawn the full formation so the gym remains usable without reloading the scene.

## Users

- **Player / tester exercising an enemy gym** — wants continuous targets to practice flight, aiming, and weapon feel without manually refreshing the scene.
- **Developer / AI agent verifying enemy behaviour** — wants a deterministic, observable wipe → countdown → respawn loop that can be asserted in automated tests.

### Example user stories

- As a **player in any enemy gym**, when I destroy the last alive enemy, I see a 3-second countdown (e.g. centred `Respawning in 3…2…1…`) and then a fresh formation appears at its starting position so I can keep shooting.
- As a **developer**, I want the wipe detection and respawn to live in the shared core (`GymFormationScene`) so all five formation gyms inherit it without per-scene duplication, and the behaviour is covered by scene tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Wipe detection and 3s countdown:** When `aliveCount` transitions to `0` (all `FormationSceneEntity.alive === false`), the scene starts a 3-second countdown and displays a visible countdown indicator (text overlay). The countdown ticks once per second and is observable for tests (getter or text contents).
- [ ] **AC2 — Automatic respawn after countdown:** After exactly 3 seconds (within tick tolerance), the full formation respawns: `aliveCount` returns to `config.count`, entities reappear at `config.startX/startY`-derived positions, formation base resets to its start, and the countdown indicator is removed. `playSpawnSound()` (or equivalent) is triggered on respawn. Enemy bullets in flight are cleared so a stale bullet does not instantly hit the player.
- [ ] **AC3 — Applies to all formation gyms via the core library:** `GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm` all exhibit AC1–AC2 with no per-scene duplication beyond config. The change is implemented in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (new fields/methods optional and backward compatible). `GymBoss` (multi-phase boss, separate scene) is out of scope unless explicitly noted.
- [ ] **AC4 — Combat and chrome preserved:** Player ship (arrows + WASD), `EXPLODE` / `SHOOT: ON/OFF` buttons, status/hint lines, drift/respawn off the right edge, and existing collision/explosion VFX/SFX behaviour remain unchanged except for the wipe→respawn addition. `shootEnabled` state carries over across the respawn (no surprise toggle).
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing and full suite:** Automated tests cover wipe detection, countdown progression (including that the countdown restarts correctly if the scene is torn down), successful respawn with correct positions/count, bullet cleanup on respawn, and that the existing `GymFormationScene` / per-gym tests still pass. Full project test suite passes (`npm test`).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` updated to document the wipe → 3s countdown → respawn convention (including that it is core-library owned); related comments updated.

## Constraints

- No game-over, lives, or scoring changes — gyms remain demo/testbeds (infinite lives, as with player hit/respawn at `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5s`).
- No collision engine — continue manual distance checks for any new collision-adjacent work.
- Prefer core-library extension over per-scene boilerplate; keep `EnemyFormationConfig` backward compatible.
- Use existing sounds (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and existing entity `destroySelf()`/`alive` contract; do not introduce a new entity type.

## Existing state

- Five enemy gyms are thin `GymFormationScene<TEntity,TBullet>` subclasses driven by `EnemyFormationConfig` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`): formation spawn, HUD buttons, status/hint/`← INDEX`, drift + `_respawnX()` off the right edge, per-entity `applyFormationPosition()`, fire-bullet collection + advance + cull, player spawn/input/auto-fire/bullet lifecycle/collisions/invulnerability blink.
- Enemies are 1 HP; destroying the last one leaves `aliveCount === 0` with no recovery — the scene stays empty indefinitely.
- Existing tests live in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/Gym*.test.ts`; player hit/respawn is already covered (explosion VFX, `respawn()`, blink).

## Desired change

- Extend `GymFormationScene` to detect `aliveCount === 0`, start and tick a 3-second countdown (visible text, deterministic via `tick(dt)`), then on expiry clear enemy bullets, destroy/recreate or resurrect the formation at its initial geometry, reset `formationBaseX/Y` to `startX/Y`, refresh `statusText`, hide the countdown, and play the spawn sound. Expose minimal test seams (e.g. `isRespawnCountdownActive()`, `getRespawnCountdownRemaining()` or equivalent).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2–§3 to note the wipe/respawn lifecycle.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Add wipe detection, 3s countdown state/tick, countdown text overlay, bullet cleanup, and formation respawn logic; expose test getters.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Add AC1–AC3 tests for the core library.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts` (and `GymDiver.ts`, `GymTank.ts`, `GymPhaser.ts`, `GymSwarm.ts`) — No code change expected, but verify via per-scene smoke/regression tests that the core behaviour is inherited.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Document the wipe → countdown → respawn convention.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Reuse `playSpawnSound()` on respawn (no change unless a distinct sound is desired).

## Related work

- **AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT** — Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (completed, parent of the combat interactions `destroySelf()`/`alive` that define "killed").
- **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH / AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** — Core scene: collision detection and player hit/respawn (establishes `aliveCount`, manual collisions, `Player.respawn()` pattern to reuse).
- **AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 / AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9 / AH-0MTAN4T0I004H187** — Core-library extraction and rewrites that make this a one-place change.
- **AH-0MT99* family** — `Create E1–E5 Enemy Gym Scene` items (consumers of the core contract).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Killed" means `alive === false` after `destroySelf()` (including explosion VFX still playing) — i.e. `aliveCount === 0` is the wipe signal, not graphics lifecycle. Mitigation: state this explicitly and assert on `aliveCount`.
- **Assumption:** 3s countdown is wall-clock seconds driven by `tick(dt)` / `time.now`, not frames, and is **visible** to the player (centred countdown text). If the producer prefers a silent timer or a different presentation, adjust the overlay without changing the timing contract. Recorded as open clarification below.
- **Assumption:** Respawn resets the formation to `startX/startY` with the original `count/spacing` geometry and clears enemy bullets only (player bullets persist). If producer wants player bullets cleared or score/status preservation, note as follow-up.
- **Risk:** Countdown races with the formation drift `_respawnX()` (right-edge respawn) — they are orthogonal. Mitigation: wipe/respawn resets `formationBaseX/Y` and does not interfere with the drift timer.
- **Risk:** Scope creep — adding scoring waves, lives, or boss waves. Mitigation: this item is strictly wipe → 3s → same formation; any wave/score work goes to a linked follow-up.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the 3-second countdown be visible to the player, and if so where/how (e.g. centred text `Respawning in 3…`, status line countdown, both)?" — Answer: **Assumed visible centred countdown text** (e.g. `Respawning in 3…` ticking to `1…`) plus status line update; change presentation if producer prefers differently. Source: researcher inference from seed text ("3 second countdown") — no prior worklog entry specifies presentation; left as producer-reviewable assumption.
- Q: "On respawn, should the formation reset to `startX/startY` (as on initial `create()`) or continue from its current drift position? Should `shootEnabled` and any per-entity state be preserved or reset?" — Answer: **Assumed full reset to start position with `shootEnabled` preserved**, fresh entities (or resurrected) at initial offsets. Source: prior gym convention (spawn at `startX/startY`) and minimal-surprise principle; flagged for producer confirmation.
- Q: "Should enemy bullets (and/or player bullets) be cleared when the countdown ends and the formation respawns?" — Answer: **Assumed enemy bullets cleared, player bullets kept**. Source: prevents a stale enemy bullet from hitting the freshly respawned player; avoids surprising the player by deleting their shots. Flagged for producer review.
- Q: "Does this apply to `GymBoss` or only the five formation gyms? Does 'killed' include mid-explosion (`alive === false` but explosion animating) or only after animation completes?" — Answer: **Assumed formation gyms only (`GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`/`GymPhaser`/`GymSwarm`); 'killed' = `aliveCount === 0` (mid-explosion counts)**. Source: Boss is multi-phase and tracked separately (`AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE` family); `alive` contract from `GymFormationScene`.

# Power ups need to be larger — Intake Brief (AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4)

## Problem statement

Power-up drops are too small and visually inconspicuous, making them difficult to pick up during play. Players need drops to be twice as large with a clearly visible glowing bubble (circle) around each drop so pickups are immediately legible and more forgiving to collect.

## Users

- **Players** — struggle to collect small drops under fire; benefit from larger, high-contrast pickups that are easier to see and overlap.
- **Gym testers / developers** — need the sizing and bubble semantics defined once so every drop type renders consistently.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want power-up drops to be twice as large so I can collect them without pixel-perfect positioning.
- As a **player**, I want each drop surrounded by a glowing bubble/circle so I can spot it instantly against the black background and busy bullet patterns.
- As a **developer**, I want the size and bubble defined as tunable constants / shared visuals so GymPowerUps and GymWeapons both render the same way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Drops are twice as large:** `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE` and `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` (canonical in `src/core/constants.ts`) are doubled from 16 → 32 px (or equivalent scale factor of 2×). All drop types use the new size, including non-combat (P5, P8, P9) and weapon (Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset). Mirrored/re-exported constants (`src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`, gym scenes) remain consistent.
- [ ] **AC2 — Glowing bubble around every drop:** Each on-field drop renders a glowing circle/bubble surrounding its icon. The bubble is code-drawn (Phaser Graphics, no external assets), in the neon style (e.g., per-type aura colour or white with outer glow), centred at the drop position and scaled with the lifecycle scale (grow/hold/shrink). GymPowerUps renders the bubble (currently no drop graphics — must add) and GymWeapons adds the bubble alongside its existing weapon icon graphics.
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection remains correct and more forgiving:** Overlap collection (`_overlapsShip` in both gym scenes) uses the new size (`DROP_SIZE * currentScale + hull`) so the effective pickup radius is doubled at full scale. Drops are still gated by the >3% collection threshold; collecting plays the existing per-type audio.
- [ ] **AC4 — Lifecycle visuals scale correctly:** Bubble + icon scale 0 → 1 → 0 with the `PowerUp` lifecycle (`advance()`) so the growing/shrinking animation remains smooth and framerate-independent; fully despawned drops remove their graphics.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation:** Existing drop/collection/magnet/weapon suites still pass with the new size (overlap thresholds updated where they hard-code 16). At least one new or updated test asserts: (a) the doubled size constant, (b) the bubble graphics are created per drop and scaled with lifecycle, (c) overlap distance at full scale is doubled. Manual visual check in GymPowerUps and GymWeapons shows the bubble clearly.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Code-first, no external art assets — bubble is drawn with Phaser Graphics / lineStyle primitives (neon vector aesthetic, GDD §7.1).
- Engine: Phaser v4 + TypeScript; web + Windows binary compatible (GDD §6.3).
- Tunable size lives in `src/core/constants.ts` (single source of truth); scenes and `src/powerups/` re-export or import from there.
- Do not change effect semantics, lifetimes, spawn cadence, or magnet math — only size and visuals.

## Existing state

- `src/core/constants.ts` defines `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE = 16` and `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE = POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE`; `HUD.ts` draws HUD icons at size 8 (not in scope).
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` draws per-type power-up icons (`drawPowerUpIcon`) and weapon icons (`drawWeaponIcon`) at the caller-supplied size; no bubble is drawn today.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` tracks `ActiveDrop { powerUp, x, y }` with no per-drop Graphics — drops have no on-screen visuals beyond lifecycle bookkeeping. Overlap uses `POWER_UP_DROP_SIZE * currentScale + hull`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` creates a `Graphics` per weapon drop, draws the weapon icon at `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE`, and scales it with `currentScale`; no bubble.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` / `effects.ts` / `spawner.ts` are size-agnostic (lifecycle is time-based, not px-based).

## Desired change

1. Double the canonical drop size constant (16 → 32) in `src/core/constants.ts`; ensure `WEAPON_DROP_SIZE` follows and re-exports stay consistent.
2. Add a glowing bubble visual for every on-field drop:
   - Introduce or extend a shared helper (e.g., in `src/powerups/icons.ts` or a small visuals helper) that draws a neon circle/bubble around the icon.

# Diver rotates to face the player and dives towards them (AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX)

## Problem statement

The Diver entity currently dives straight down (x locked at formation slot) regardless of where the player is. It should rotate to visually face the player and dive along a trajectory that targets the player's position at dive start.

## Users

- **Player:** Divers that intelligently target the player's position create more engaging and threatening enemy behaviour, consistent with the GDD's vision of the Diver as a diving threat.
- **Developer:** The change is contained within the Diver entity's state machine, with minimal impact on the gym scene or other entities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Visual rotation to face the player:** During the formation hold phase (before diving), the Diver rotates its body to visually point toward the player's position. The rotation is smooth and updates each frame.
- **AC2 — Dive trajectory targets player position at dive start:** The Diver's dive parabolic arc targets the player's position at the moment the dive starts (snapshot, not live tracking). The x-coordinate is no longer locked — the diver moves diagonally along the parabolic path from formation slot to player position.
- **AC3 — Formation movement unchanged:** The Diver's formation movement (drifting, idle wiggle) remains unchanged from current behaviour — movement perpendicular to facing direction during non-diving phases.
- **AC4 — Existing dive timing and return preserved:** The dive duration (~2 s), hold time (~3 s), and return-to-formation logic are unchanged.
- **AC5 — All tests pass:** All existing gym tests pass. AC1 test (AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB) that asserts x is locked during dive must be updated to reflect the new diagonal dive behaviour.

## Constraints

- **Single-file change:** All changes are contained in `src/entities/Diver.ts` only.
- **Backward compatible:** The `setAimTarget()` seam and existing public API are preserved.
- **No scene changes:** The gym scene (`GymDiver.ts`) requires no modifications.

## Existing state

- Diver dives in a vertical parabolic arc (x locked at `_diveStartX`, y follows the curve).
- The dart sprite is drawn pointing "down" (nose at bottom of the dart shape) but has no rotation applied.
- AC1 from AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB asserts x-coordinate remains constant during dive.
- The `_drawBody()` method draws the dart in a fixed orientation (nose at `half` y, i.e., bottom of local space).

## Desired change

1. **Rotation:** Add a rotation property to the Diver that smoothly rotates the container toward the player during the formation hold phase. The `_drawBody()` method should be updated so the dart's nose points "up" (negative y in local space) so that positive rotation aligns the nose toward the target.
2. **Dive trajectory:** Remove the x-lock in `_handleDive()`. The dive should use the full quadratic bezier: x moves from `_diveStartX` through `_diveApexX` to `_diveTargetX` (the player's position at dive start). Y follows the same curve.
3. **Test update:** Update the AC1 test that currently asserts x is constant during dive — it should now assert that the diver moves along the expected diagonal parabolic path.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — Add rotation to face player during hold; modify `_handleDive` to use full bezier for both x and y.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymDiver.test.ts` — Update AC1 dive x-constant test to expect diagonal movement.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB** (completed): "Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to current formation slot" — established the x-lock. This work item supersedes that fix.
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH** (open): "Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking" — includes AC2 about Diver dive targeting player live position. This work item uses a snapshot (at dive start), consistent with AC2's recorded decision.
- **AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD** (completed): "Diver jumps on return from dive" — related return-from-dive fix.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing the dive trajectory may affect the visual balance of the gym scene (diagonal dives vs vertical). If the arc is too aggressive, divers may be too easy to dodge. Mitigation: use the same parabolic parameters (apex at 30% screen height) — only the horizontal component changes.
- **Risk:** The sprite rotation approach (rotating the container vs rotating the draw method) needs testing to ensure the explosion animation and bullet spawning still work correctly with rotated dividers.
- **Assumption:** The dart shape is drawn in local coordinates, so rotating the container rotates the entire diver (body, explosion, etc.).
- **Assumption:** The existing `setAimTarget()` seam is used to provide the target position at dive start. The scene already calls this per-frame.
- **Scope creep:** This does NOT include live re-targeting mid-dive (that is AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH AC2). Only the dive-start snapshot is implemented here.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should we remove the x-lock during dive?" — Answer: Yes, movement is along the dive path (no movement perpendicular to it). Source: operator reply 1.
- Q: "What does 'right angles to facing' apply to?" — Answer: Non-diving movement only. During the dive, movement is towards the player. Source: operator reply 2.
- Q: "Does rotate to face the player include trajectory or just visuals?" — Answer: Both — visual rotation AND the dive trajectory follows toward the player's position. Source: operator reply 3.

# Implement: Wipe detection, 3s countdown, and respawn in GymFormationScene (AH-0MTCORE01)

## Summary

Extend GymFormationScene to detect when all enemies are destroyed (aliveCount === 0), show a 3-second visible countdown, then respawn the full formation at its starting position.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 - Wipe detection:** When aliveCount transitions to 0 (all enemies alive === false), the scene immediately enters the respawn countdown state.
- [ ] **AC2 - 3s visible countdown:** A centered text overlay displays "Respawning in 3...", "Respawning in 2...", "Respawning in 1...", ticking once per second. The countdown is driven by tick(dt) with wall-clock seconds.
- [ ] **AC3 - Automatic respawn:** After exactly 3 seconds, the full formation respawns: all entities recreated at config.startX/startY-derived positions, formationBaseX/Y reset, aliveCount returns to config.count, countdown text removed.
- [ ] **AC4 - Bullet cleanup:** On respawn, all enemy bullets in flight are destroyed and cleared. Player bullets persist.
- [ ] **AC5 - Sound & state:** playSpawnSound() is called on respawn. shootEnabled state carries over (preserved across respawn).
- [ ] **AC6 - Test seams:** Expose isRespawnCountdownActive(): boolean and getRespawnCountdownRemaining(): number as public getters for test observation.
- [ ] **AC7 - No breaking changes:** All existing gym scenes continue to work unchanged; existing tests still pass.

## Implementation Notes

- Add new fields to GymFormationScene: private respawnCountdown = 0, private isRespawning = false, private countdownText: Phaser.GameObjects.Text
- In tick(dt): after the existing drift/bullet logic, check if aliveCount === 0 and not already respawning - set isRespawning = true, respawnCountdown = 3, create/hide the countdown text overlay.
- During countdown: decrement respawnCountdown by dt; update countdownText each second to show "Respawning in {N}...".
- When respawnCountdown <= 0: destroy old entities (call destroy() on each), clear this.bullets, recreate the formation via config.buildOffsets() + config.createEntity() loop (same as create()), reset formationBaseX/Y, hide countdown text, play playSpawnSound().
- The countdown overlay should be positioned at GAME_WIDTH/2, GAME_HEIGHT/2 with appropriate style matching gym HUD.
- EnemyFormationConfig is backward compatible - no new required fields.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts - Add wipe detection, countdown state/tick, overlay text, bullet cleanup, formation respawn logic, and test getters.

## Dependencies

- None - this is the core implementation work item.
